subject: Clarify SLA: uptime measurement, response tiers, and maintenance scope
messages:
From: Sara Lin <sara.lin@finntech.io>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-04-21T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: FinnTech redlines - SLA and maintenance scope

Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Attached are FinnTech's legal redlines on the MSA and Order Form focused on the service guarantee and maintenance carveouts. High-level items we flagged: 

- Uptime metric definition: your current wording averages across a month; we want clarification that planned maintenance and brief rolling restarts are explicitly excluded and that measurement is based on per-minute availability per region.
- Service credits: the formula in Section 4.2 isn't aligned with our procurement policy; we asked for a flat credit for each percentage bucket rather than a pro-rata token calculation.
- Response SLAs: we need guaranteed P1 response within 1 hour and P2 within 8 hours.
- Maintenance windows: propose a maximum of 4 hours per calendar month for scheduled maintenance affecting production, with at least 72-hour notice and an explicit carveout for emergency security patches that require less notice but limited to 2 events / year.

Please confirm whether Redwood can accept these redlines or if you want to propose alternate language. We can loop in our technical contact (cc'ed) if helpful.

Attachments: FinnTech_MSA_Redline_20260420.pdf (redline), OrderForm_v3_marked.docx (tracked changes)

Regards,
Sara Lin
Head of Procurement, FinnTech

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: Sara Lin <sara.lin@finntech.io>
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.ai, irene_choi@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-04-21T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: FinnTech redlines - SLA and maintenance scope

Sara — thanks for sending this over and for the clear redlines. High level we think we can meet the intent but need to align on measurable definitions so there are no surprises in production. Key notes from our side: 

- Uptime measurement: Redwood typically measures uptime at a per-region, per-hour granularity and excludes scheduled maintenance windows and any customer-isolated configuration windows. We can accept language that excludes scheduled maintenance (with notice) and brief rolling restarts under 5 minutes per instance, but we need to keep per-hour aggregation to avoid spurious credits from micro-bursts.
- Credits: Redwood prefers a capped monthly credit pool with percentage buckets (e.g., 5% of monthly fees for <99.5%, up to 100% cap). We understand FinnTech prefers flat credits per bucket — we can propose a hybrid: discrete credit tiers with a hard cap.
- Response times: P1 1 hour is aggressive but doable for Dedicated contracts; for Hosted customers we commit to 1 hour for platform-wide incidents and 2 hours for account-targeted P1. Would you be open to matching on Dedicated / Hosted distinctions?
- Maintenance: we can provide a max of 4 hours per month for customer-impacting scheduled maintenance, 72-hour notice, and allow emergency security patches as you requested but limited to 3 per year (we propose 3 rather than 2 given infrastructure realities).

I'll pull in Aditya (ops) and Irene (legal) to draft alternate language and a marked-up clause set. Proposed next step: internal review + technical confirmation, then we send back a single redline. Would you prefer a phone call to walk through the measurement math?

Best,
Marissa
Director, Customer Success — Redwood Inference

From: aditya_rao@redwood.ai
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, irene_choi@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-04-22T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: FW: FinnTech redlines - SLA and maintenance scope

Marissa / Irene — forwarding FinnTech's redlines. My quick ops POV: 

- Measurement: per-region per-hour aggregation is standard for our telemetry. If legal insists on per-minute availability, we should require that credits trigger only after a continuous outage window (e.g., 5 consecutive minutes aggregated across N replicas) to avoid noisy signals.
- Rolling restarts: we can guarantee that rolling restarts will not cause more than 2 minutes of unavailability per replica; however, cumulative impact across hundreds of replicas could look worse to an external metric. Recommend we keep 'excludes brief rolling restarts under 5m per replica, and credits only for >5m sustained region-wide outages'.
- Credits formula: ops prefers a simple tiered approach (easier to explain to customers). Example we propose to legal: 99.95-100%: no credit; 99.5-99.95%: 10% credit; 99.0-99.5%: 25% credit; <99.0%: 50% credit, monthly cap 100% of monthly fees. This avoids token-level accounting complexity.
- Emergency maintenance: limit to 3 events / year for guaranteed immediate action; for transparency we will post event summaries.

I'll help draft language on the outage aggregation and the sustained-window threshold. Marissa — if you agree I can produce a short clause set for Irene to fold into the Order Form redline.

- Aditya
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

From: irene_choi@redwood.ai
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, aditya_rao@redwood.ai, Sara Lin <sara.lin@finntech.io>
Date: 2026-04-23T11:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: FinnTech redlines - SLA and maintenance scope

Sara / Marissa / Aditya — thanks for the clear thread. We've drafted proposed language and attached an Order Form excerpt that reconciles FinnTech's asks with Redwood's operational constraints. Highlights of our proposed text: 

1) "Availability Measurement": Availability will be measured per-region using per-minute telemetry aggregated into hourly windows for the purposes of credit calculation. Scheduled maintenance (defined below) and brief rolling restarts (defined as instance-level restarts with <5 minutes unavailability per instance) shall be excluded from Availability calculations. Credits shall only apply where a region experiences a sustained availability loss of at least 5 consecutive minutes affecting the customer.

2) "Service Credit Tiers": We propose a tiered credit schedule (99.95-100%: 0% credit; 99.5-99.95%: 10% credit; 99.0-99.5%: 25% credit; <99.0%: 50% credit) with a monthly cap equal to 100% of the Monthly Recurring Charges. This aligns with Redwood's operational telemetry and FinnTech's need for predictability.

3) "Response Times": For Dedicated customers, Redwood will target P1 response within 1 hour and P2 within 8 hours. For Hosted customers, P1 response is target 2 hours (1 hour for platform-wide incidents) and P2 is 8 hours. Response times are measured from the time a ticket is opened in Redwood's portal and categorized using mutually-agreed severity definitions.

4) "Scheduled Maintenance & Emergency Patches": Scheduled maintenance will be limited to 4 hours per calendar month for customer-impacting work with at least 72-hour notice. Emergency security patches may be performed without 72-hour notice but will be limited to 3 such events per 12-month period; notice will be provided as soon as practicable and a post-event summary will be published.

Next steps: Marissa, if FinnTech agrees to the sustained-window threshold and the tiered credit schedule above, we can update the redline and return to Sara for final legal review. Sara — happy to hop on a 30-minute call if you'd prefer to resolve the remaining wording.

Attachments: OrderForm_SLA_Excerpt_20260423.docx (proposed text)

Irene Choi
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
